name: OpenAI Codex CLI code mode (codex-code-mode-host, V8)
engine: V8 isolate (rusty v8 with v8_enable_sandbox) in a separate codex-code-mode-host process that is spawned without Seatbelt
how_run: Python client spawns the shipped codex-code-mode-host binary and speaks its default framed-JSON stdio protocol (same handshake and capabilities as codex-rs/code-mode remote_session), opens a session with server-side output truncation as Codex core does, executes cells with one function tool `lookup`, and answers tool/invoke delegate requests; no model.

defaults.time: none; cells yield to the caller after 10 s (DEFAULT_EXEC_YIELD_TIME_MS) and keep running until terminated or interrupted
defaults.memory: none enforced; V8 default heap (~1.4 GB observed) then fatal OOM of the host process
defaults.output: 10,000 tokens per exec call by default (DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_PER_EXEC_CALL), truncated with a warning header; 1 MiB bounded-output cap on the wire
defaults.tool_calls: no count limit observed; capability 'delegate-capacity-4096' advertises 4,096 concurrent delegate requests

source_notes.finding: Generated: Codex renders a TypeScript declaration `declare const tools: { name(args: {...}): Promise<...> }` from each tool's JSON Schema into the exec tool description; in V8 each enabled tool becomes a function on the `tools` object, named by normalize_code_mode_identifier.

Upfront by default (all enabled tools declared in the description, plus an ALL_TOOLS global); feature code_mode_tool_search adds ranked in-code search, and code_mode_only hides direct tools behind exec/wait.

Separate host process. Core and host exchange u32-length-prefixed JSON frames over stdio (or gRPC over stdio). A tools.x() call becomes a delegate/request tool/invoke frame to Codex core, which runs the tool through its normal router and answers with delegate/response.

V8 isolate with the V8 sandbox build flag; console, Atomics, SharedArrayBuffer and WebAssembly are deleted; imports are rejected. The host process itself is spawned with plain Command (no Seatbelt), with Codex-internal tokens scrubbed from its env.

Only what the cell emits through text()/image()/content() returns as content_items, plus error_text. Server-side truncation to max_output_tokens (default 10,000) with a 'Warning: truncated output' header.

The protocol carries max_heap_size_bytes, but CodeModeService::with_options overwrites it with None and the runtime creates isolates with default CreateParams, so no heap cap is applied (only the UI engine gets 64 MB). No wall-clock limit; yield_time_ms only controls when the caller gets a Yielded snapshot.
Fresh V8 context per cell; a session-level key/value store (store/load) is snapshotted into each cell.
Uncaught errors return as content 'Script error:\n<message + stack>' and error_text, with exec_main.mjs line:col.

Feature `code_mode` is stage UnderDevelopment and default off; sub-flags select the standalone host, gRPC transport, prewarm, interrupt handling and code-mode-only. Async: top-level await, Promise.all, setTimeout and notify() are available.

surprises: Codex was briefed as having no code mode; codex-cli 0.169.0 ships one (codex-code-mode-host, 70 MB V8 binary) behind the `code_mode` feature flag.

max_heap_size_bytes is part of the wire protocol and the host advertises 'session-cell-execution-resource-limits', yet service.rs forces the heap limit to None; an allocation loop crashes the entire host process (P7).
No execution time limit: a busy loop keeps a cell alive indefinitely and only yields observations every 10 s (P6).
The code-mode host runs outside Seatbelt; the only boundary for model-written JS is the V8 isolate, while shell commands get Seatbelt.
A bare final expression is discarded; output must go through text() (console is deleted) (P2).

hardened.config: No Codex config key, host CLI flag or env var sets a time or heap limit: [features.code_mode] only has default_exec_yield_time_ms, experimental_show_cell_overhead, tool_input_schema_max_bytes, excluded_tool_namespaces, direct_only_tool_namespaces (features/src/feature_configs.rs:38-60); codex-code-mode-host takes only --listen and --otel-trace-listen/--otel-trace-exporter (code-mode-host/src/main.rs:20-43); Codex core always opens sessions with default (empty) limits (core/src/code_mode_host.rs:64-66, core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs:257). So the strictest public knobs are the host's stdio protocol fields, sent directly: session/open cellExecutionLimits {maxHeapSizeBytes: 67108864 (64 MiB, chosen), maxYieldTimeMs: 1000 (chosen)} (code-mode-protocol/src/host/payload.rs:26-31, host/message.rs:186-194), outputTruncation server; session/execute yield_time_ms 1000, max_output_tokens 1000 (payload.rs:205-211). The host advertises session-cell-execution-resource-limits and replies session/ready, then drops the heap limit (code-mode-runtime/src/service.rs:59-71 sets max_heap_size_bytes: None; isolates use CreateParams::default, runtime/mod.rs:191), so it counts as absent. maxYieldTimeMs only caps when the caller gets a Yielded snapshot (service.rs:257-270). session/terminate is a real kill (out/codemode/hardened-P6-terminate.txt) but only on request: core sends it when the model calls wait with terminate:true (core/src/tools/code_mode/wait_handler.rs:129) or the user interrupts (core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs:171), so it is not a limit. Paths relative to research/impls/codex-sandbox/src/codex-rs (tag rust-v0.169.0).
